item.title: Apple debuts iPhone Duo, its first foldable, at $1,999 (5 minute read)
item.description: New CEO John Ternus led his first keynote, headlined by the iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable, a passport-style device with a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display that automatically reflows apps based on how the phone is folded, starting at $1,999. Apple also unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max ($1,199/$1,299, up $100 from last year) with new A20 Pro processors, a variable mechanical aperture camera, and 24-30 hour battery life, alongside the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, which add a 5-second heart rate sensor Apple claims is more accurate than a chest strap.

item.title: OpenAI may double-source next-gen AI chips at Samsung, alongside TSMC (3 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI Korea GM Harrison Kim revealed the company has made real progress with Samsung Electronics on joint production and research for its next-generation chips, expanding a relationship that so far has been mostly about memory supply and enterprise software. OpenAI's current inference ASIC, Jalapeño, was designed with Broadcom and built at TSMC in under 18 months and is already in mass production there, so any Samsung involvement more plausibly targets its successor, which is reportedly approaching tapeout.

item.title: Introducing CUDA Rust for High-Performance GPU Kernel Development (5 minute read)
item.description: NVIDIA has announced CUDA Rust and introduced two specialized compilation tracks that allow developers to author and optimize GPU compute kernels directly in Rust. This release brings Rust's strong compile-time memory safety guarantees and modern tooling ecosystem to GPU-accelerated workloads. Developers implementing embedded vision, intensive sensor fusion, and real-time state estimation on mobile platforms can now exploit GPU compute power while minimizing memory-related crashes and runtime concurrency bugs.

item.title: TSMC's August revenue jumps 53% to a record high, plans High-NA EUV adoption for 2030 (3 minute read)
item.description: TSMC posted NT$514.8 billion ($16.1 billion) in August revenue, up 53.3% year-over-year and 10.1% from July, hitting a fresh monthly record as AI-driven chip demand keeps outpacing supply. It came alongside a separate announcement with Dutch equipment maker ASML: TSMC plans to bring ASML's High-NA EUV lithography into large-scale manufacturing starting in 2030 for its most advanced nodes, as AI accelerators push toward increasingly complex transistor architectures.

item.title: Besxar flies first suborbital semiconductor manufacturing demo, banking on free vacuum in space (2 minute read)
item.description: Besxar, a $9.35 million seed-funded startup, flew its first mission on July 5 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 alongside a Starlink batch, carrying its own semiconductor wafers plus test wafers from the University of Virginia and UT Austin. The company's pitch is simple: Earth-based fabs spend billions on pumps to create the vacuum semiconductors need, but in space vacuum is free, so Besxar wants to manufacture higher-quality, lower-cost wafers in orbit and return them to Earth to sell.

item.title: vLLM triples MiniMax M3 inference throughput on AMD's MI355X through systematic bottleneck chasing (6 minute read)
item.description: AMD and Embedded LLM teams took MiniMax M3's day-0 vLLM implementation from 109.1 to 342.4 output tokens/s/GPU on AMD's Instinct MI355X, a 3.14x gain, by repeatedly asking five questions as the bottleneck kept shifting: what local shape reached each rank after tensor-parallel sharding, what work repeats every layer, which bytes actually move, whether a claimed fast path actually executed, and which queue grows once kernels stop being the limiter. Big wins came from fusing the model's shared expert into the same grouped GEMMs as routed experts (up to 30% faster at low concurrency), and reusing sparse-attention block selections across adjacent layers instead of recomputing per layer.

item.title: LG denies claims its smart TVs constantly record and upload audio (4 minute read)
item.description: Gamers Nexus published a two-hour investigation, done with security researchers MrBruh and uturn using packet capture and firmware analysis, alleging LG's smart TVs constantly log and upload user data even offline or in standby, scan local Wi-Fi networks for other devices, and record and store ambient audio through the TV's microphone for later retrieval, even when the TV appears off. LG called the claims untrue, saying its TVs only process voice data when the remote's voice button is pressed or its "Hi LG" wake word is detected after a user manually enables far-field voice recognition, with wake-word audio processed entirely on-device and deleted immediately if no match is found.

item.title: Google commits $15B to Finland data centers, explores nuclear power for the buildout (3 minute read)
item.description: Google plans to invest at least $15 billion in Finnish AI infrastructure through 2028, its largest single investment in Europe, building on over 15 years of presence there. Alongside the buildout, Google signed a 22-year power agreement with Finnish utility Fortum and said it will explore business models that could support new nuclear reactors at Fortum's Loviisa site, tying the compute expansion directly to a long-term power source.

item.title: Huawei and Cambricon hike AI chip prices 20-50% as HBM shortage forces grey-market buying (3 minute read)
item.description: Chinese AI chipmakers, including Huawei and Cambricon, have sharply raised prices for current and next-gen processors.

item.title: Covenant unveils Anthem, a heavy-payload strike missile built to be mass-produced across three countries (3 minute read)
item.description: Anthem is a long-range precision strike weapon aimed at a gap Covenant argues current Western arsenals lack.

item.title: XPENG's IRON humanoid walks off its new automotive-grade production line (3 minute read)
item.description: XPENG commissioned its humanoid robot production lines, and its IRON robot autonomously walked off them after completing assembly, a step the company frames as moving from R&D prototypes to real line manufacturing.

item.title: Analog Devices pays $1.35B for edge AI chipmaker Alif Semiconductor (4 minute read)
item.description: Analog Devices agreed to buy Alif Semiconductor for $1.35 billion cash plus up to $200 million contingent on performance, adding microcontrollers built to run neural networks directly on-device rather than sending data to a data center.

item.title: JD.com plans 3 million robots and a 100,000-accelerator Physical AI cluster (5 minute read)
item.description: JD Logistics plans to procure 3 million robots, 1 million autonomous vehicles, and 100,000 delivery drones over five years to automate picking, sorting, transport, and last-mile delivery.

item.title: Vention opens a Physical AI lab tied directly to thousands of factories (5 minute read)
item.description: Vention opened a Montreal lab focused on robotic manipulation, industrial data collection, and post-training robotics foundation models using learning-from-demonstration, reinforcement learning, vision models, and motion planning.

item.title: Dreamforce starts in 5 days. Stream it all live, for free (Sponsor)
item.description: From accelerating vulnerability detection to creating observability headaches, AI is putting security teams to the test. That's why protecting data, governing AI agents, and building securely at scale are core focuses at Dreamforce.The Security Keynote lays out how to outpace evolving threats and accelerate AI with trust, visibility, and guardrails. Then, the AIforce Keynotewill break down how business logic and governance can power intelligent experiences everywhere.Register for free to stream Dreamforce live on Salesforce+.

item.title: ClearFake WebDAV Infection Chain Delivers Amatera Stealer, ZigCryptoStealer, and NetSupport Manager (17 minute read)
item.description: Cisco Talos identified two WebDAV-based infection chains delivering the Amatera Stealer to facilitate untargeted credential and cryptocurrency theft. The initial chain executed a DLL named "verification.google" at a Ukrainian government organization. A parallel "pf.ch" chain used ClearFake JavaScript stored on the BNB Smart Chain, alongside a fake Google CAPTCHA ClickFix prompt, to task secondary payloads, including ZigCryptoStealer and NetSupport Manager.

item.title: Adobe Commerce max-severity bug comes under active attack (3 minute read)
item.description: Threat actors are actively exploiting CVE-2026-75650, a max-severity unauthenticated code execution vulnerability dubbed StyleSmuggler, to compromise online stores running Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source. Exploitation began on September 4, with the deployment of a Rust backdoor and a separate PHP web shell. Adobe released emergency hotfix VULN-393411 to address the flaw, prompting Sansec to warn that patching alone is insufficient for stores that may already be compromised.

item.title: SAP Warns of Maximum Severity OVERPASS Kernel Vulnerability (2 minute read)
item.description: German software company SAP has released an update that patches 20 security vulnerabilities. Of particular note is a maximum-severity buffer overflow vulnerability in the External Passport Protocol (EPP) processing library, which could allow an unprivileged attacker to run arbitrary commands as an administrator. Another missing authentication vulnerability in the SAP NetWeaver Message Server could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious payloads and arbitrary commands across the full SAP system cluster.

item.title: CVE-2026-82533: DeepSeek Harness Vulnerability Lets AI Agents Escape Their Own Sandbox (6 minute read)
item.description: CVE-2026-82533 affects DeepSeek Harness 0.1.1-rc.2 and earlier. Its local API trusted the client-controlled Host header instead of the peer address. Sandboxed sessions retained loopback access and could call that API to enable danger-full-access with approvals disabled. A single shell command escaped the sandbox on default settings. If port 3080 was forwarded or tunneled, unauthenticated remote attackers could control sessions and export stored conversations. DeepSeek fixed the issue in 0.1.2-alpha.1.

item.title: GTIG AI Threat Tracker: From Prompting to Autonomy – The Evolution of Adversarial AI (22 minute read)
item.description: Google's GTIG reports that threat actors have graduated from basic prompting to agentic AI workflows that autonomously manage scanning pipelines, resolve errors, and execute multi-stage attacks with minimal human oversight, compressing response windows from days to hours. For instance, groups like UNC6780 exploit the AI supply chain by stealing GitHub Actions tokens to sign malicious packages by tricking LLMs, state-sponsored groups use AI across the full attack lifecycle from reconnaissance to post-exploitation, and financially motivated actors built credential-harvesting agents that stole thousands of secrets in under six hours using only AI coding tools and markdown playbooks.

item.title: Untracked Nightmares: The Threats Hiding Behind Commodity Infrastructure (14 minute read)
item.description: Unit 42 traced two routine-looking adware infections to CL-CRI-1171, a pay-per-install operation that has run for two years behind a shared loader called OfferLoader, delivering payloads through 11 gaming-optimization YouTube channels and an SEO-poisoning funnel into corporate and government endpoints. The loader gates delivery on a Base64 click_id fingerprint of OS, browser, referrer, search keyword, and IP, so scanners and analysts get a decoy download page while real victims get the payload, which explains the near-zero public footprint despite 10,000+ loader samples and 200+ rotating domains. Defenders should stop triaging commodity loader alerts as low priority and pivot on loader C2 infrastructure instead, since a single OfferLoader run here spawned three unrelated campaigns including a cross-platform Insomnia RAT, a steganography-delivered WebSocket tunneler, and a Chrome Secure Preferences bypass.

item.title: Your team is using AI. Help them secure it with Datadog's guide (Sponsor)
item.description: Cybersecurity was already a mess before AI. Now it's harder than ever to keep up. This Datadog guide lays out how AI works, its entry points and business logic, and the underlying components that host and run LLM apps. It also provides tactical steps you can take to improve AI security today. Get the guide

item.title: Privileged Identity and Access in Microsoft Entra (GitHub Repo)
item.description: A collection of docs, resources, and samples for implementing secure, privileged IAM in Microsoft Azure and Entra.

item.title: Kontext (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Kontext puts local policy between AI agents and the tools they call. It observes supported actions, evaluates policy before consequential actions run, and records the decision and outcome in an authorization ledger.

item.title: Cymphony (Product Launch)
item.description: Cymphony maps employee and machine identities, their system access, and sensitive data exposure. It detects risky permissions, investigates incidents, prioritizes fixes, and automates access corrections.

item.title: IonQ Compiles Shor's Attack on secp256k1 Down to 19,397 Ions and 26 Days per Attempt (21 minute read)
item.description: IonQ published a blueprint estimating that 19,397 physical qubits and 1,457 logical qubits are required to break 256-bit elliptic-curve signatures and compromise dependent systems. The proposed attack uses the Walking Cat architecture to solve the secp256k1 discrete logarithm problem with about 39 million Toffoli gates over an estimated 25.7 days per attempt. IonQ describes this as the first fully compiled, fault-tolerant resource estimate for this attack and notes that the required machine does not currently exist and that the estimated scale aligns with its 2028 technology roadmap.

item.title: LG accused of 'egregious invasion of privacy' over TV data collection (3 minute read)
item.description: Gamers Nexus found LG TVs allegedly recording audio after voice features were enabled, including during standby. Tests reportedly uncovered plaintext transcripts, IP addresses, location data, nearby Wi‑Fi details, and local-device inventories. The team also alleged offline audio capture and a possible remote-code-execution flaw. LG denied ambient recording and said ACR advertising use requires opt-in consent.

item.title: Pre-Task RCE in Google Gemini CLI (CVE-2026-12537) (10 minute read)
item.description: Novee researchers disclosed a CVSS 10.0 pre-task RCE in Gemini CLI where GEMINI_SANDBOX_PROXY_COMMAND in .gemini/.env reached a host shell via spawn(..., { shell: true }) before the sandbox even started, exposing all parent process secrets (GITHUB_TOKEN, GEMINI_API_KEY) and bypassing four defensive layers. The same pre-task execution pattern appeared in Claude Code (execution before the trust dialog) and Codex (MCP auto-launch before the model), revealing a shared architectural blind spot: workspace configuration influences process authority before model-time guardrails activate. The exploit required no prompt injection—three lines in a configuration file were sufficient for host-level code execution.

item.title: Hackers Return $263 Million Stolen From Liquid Network (2 minute read)
item.description: White-hat hackers drained ~$320 million from Liquid Network's federation wallet over the weekend.

item.title: First 'Take It Down Act' Sentencing Puts Man Behind Bars for 15 Years (1 minute read)
item.description: Ohio man James Strahler received the first Take It Down Act conviction, with a 15-year sentence for distributing 3,000+ real and AI-generated child sexual abuse images and cyberstalking victims.

item.title: Think like an attacker. Prepare like a defender. (Sponsor)
item.description: What do cybercriminals look for before they strike? Former FBI Special Agent Jeff Lanza and Flexential VP of Cybersecurity Services Will Bass share lessons from real-world cases in Outsmarting cybercrime: Lessons from an FBI insider. Learn how attackers identify vulnerabilities, exploit human behavior, and gain a foothold, plus get practical insights for reducing risk, strengthening cyber resilience, and preparing your organization to respond and recover when prevention isn't enough.

item.title: WeWorm (4 minute read)
item.description: Calif has demonstrated a zero-click worm that takes over a WeChat account via an unanswered VoIP call, then uses that account to call the victim's contacts. This exploit relies on a memory corruption bug in WeChat's VoIP stack and requires the attacker to be on the victim's friend list, which is a weak barrier since one compromised friend can lead to further exploitation. Tencent has mitigated this issue in server-side updates and in client versions Android 8.0.77 and iOS 8.0.76, so users should enforce these updates and reconsider trusted-contact privileges in messaging apps.

item.title: 220M Traveler Records Exposed in Vietnam-Linked APIS Leak (2 minute read)
item.description: Security researchers gained access to an Elasticsearch cluster containing an Advanced Passenger Information System (APIS) database with records belonging to 220M passengers and flight crew members. The researchers received a 401 when trying to access the cluster via the public internet but could reach the database, which accepted default credentials via a cloud-based access path. The data includes passengers' and crew members' names, dates of birth, sex, nationalities, passport or travel document numbers, document expiration dates, and issuing countries.

item.title: Hackers Breach F5 BIG-IP APM Devices to Deploy Linux Rootkit (2 minute read)
item.description: There is a malware campaign targeting F5 BIG-IP APM devices that exploits a critical RCE vulnerability and injects a fileless web shell. A distinct installer deploys the payload by infecting the Apache executable and modifying SELinux configurations. ESET researchers identified the malware as PoisonedRefresh.

item.title: Hacking AI customer service agents (11 minute read)
item.description: Researchers demonstrated attacks against customer-support agents through email spoofing, duplicate From headers, out-of-office replies, and email-address parser mismatches. These flaws can trigger profile changes, refunds, phishing emails, or account data disclosure. Alternatively, other paths reset OTP rate limits, abuse IVR checks, and steal third-party reset codes from monitored support inboxes. Hidden instructions in alternate MIME parts, CSS-hidden text, and attacker-controlled images can mislead automated processing. Untrusted forum comments and namespace-controlled sitemap pages can also poison support knowledge bases.

item.title: RFD 301: Has anybody seen my keys?: A key-hierarchy strategy for rack-level security (12 minute read)
item.description: Oxide published its internal design for protecting rack data at rest, rooting everything in a Shamir-shared rack secret that no attacker can recover without stealing at least K sleds or M.2 drives. Per-drive ZFS wrapper keys are derived with HKDF using SHA3-256 and an info string built from the PCI vendor ID, drive model, and serial number, so compromising one disk key leaves the others intact. The harder problem is rotation across a distributed two-phase commit: the dealer encrypts the epoch N-1 rack secret under a key derived from the epoch N secret using chacha20poly1305, keeping the old secret unrecoverable until the new configuration commits.

item.title: The Shared Clipboard Inside the Sandbox: Cross-Account Data Leakage in ChatGPT (10 minute read)
item.description: Check Point Research discovered that ChatGPT code-execution containers from different accounts were using package metadata as a covert cross-account channel because these containers could read and write item properties on the same internal JFrog Artifactory instance. This allowed attackers to deliver a planted instruction through a shared conversation, a custom GPT, or a pasted prompt. The model would then run a hidden second task stream in the same turn, pulling data from the victim's connected Gmail while the visible answer stayed clean. Although OpenAI has decommissioned that Artifactory instance, defenders should enable per-session isolation for any mutable state in shared internal services and review default low-risk reads configuration.

item.title: Sage (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Sage is a security tool from Gen Digital that intercepts tool calls made by AI coding assistants and blocks dangerous ones before they execute. It features URL reputation checks against a cloud service, 300+ local YAML heuristics for risky commands and credential exposure, and two-tier prompt injection detection combining heuristics with a fine-tuned ML model. Sage is supported in many harnesses like Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, OpenClaw, and OpenCode, with npm or marketplace installs per platform.

item.title: Prism-platform (GitHub Repo)
item.description: All-in-one OSINT platform — 22+ modules, AI analysis, real-time dashboard, and OPSEC scoring. Scan domains, IPs, emails, phones, and usernames.

item.title: DecBench (Website)
item.description: DecBench is a living benchmark from Noelo Lab at the University of Georgia that scores decompilers and LLMs on exact source recovery. It measures perfect-match percentage across datasets covering control flow structure, type recovery, and recompilability, with new tools added to the leaderboard as they ship.

item.title: Fake IT Calls Target Executives in Microsoft 365 Data Theft and Extortion Attacks (2 minute read)
item.description: PREY-0058 targets executives through fake IT help-desk calls and authentication-themed domains. Its AitM pages capture Microsoft 365 credentials, MFA approvals, and session tokens. Operators replay tokens through residential proxies, then enumerate SharePoint and Entra ID. They bulk-exfiltrate SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange, and Box data before issuing extortion demands. Defenders are advised to watch for proxy token replay, mailbox harvesting, and new MFA-themed domains.

item.title: Passkeys and WebAuthn explained (8 minute read)
item.description: This walkthrough covers passkey registration and login end-to-end, from server-issued challenges and stored public keys to SimpleWebAuthn verification in Node. Phishing resistance comes from RP ID scoping, which browsers enforce, but servers must still verify alongside exact origin, challenge freshness, and user verification. Teams tend to underestimate single-use challenges, concurrent login tabs, credential management screens, and recovery paths that end up weaker than the login they back up.

item.title: UK food supply chain at risk from hostile attacks (2 minute read)
item.description: The National Audit Office named cyberattacks as a threat to the UK food supply chain. Marks & Spencer estimates its April 2025 attack cost £136 million after warehouse systems were disconnected, and the Co-op confirmed theft of 6.5 million member records. Several food supply chain organizations cited the substantial investments businesses are making to manage the threat and incidence of cyber-attacks.

item.title: Think like an attacker. Prepare like a defender. (Sponsor)
item.description: Learn how cybercriminals identify vulnerabilities, exploit human behavior, and gain a foothold in Outsmarting cybercrime: Lessons from an FBI insider, with practical insights for strengthening cyber resilience. Get the Ebook

item.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes (2 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft has released 974 patches, its largest batch ever, including two actively exploited privilege-escalation zero-days and 113 critical vulnerabilities.

item.title: Grindr pays £26m to settle UK lawsuit over allegedly sharing users' HIV status (2 minute read)
item.description: Grindr agreed to pay £26m to settle a UK privacy claim involving 12,000 users as the suit alleged pre-2020 sharing of sensitive data, including HIV status, with advertising firms.

item.title: New Android RAT uses worm to target exposed ADB services (1 minute read)
item.description: Dark Atlas has documented THost9, an Android RAT whose worm component scans for internet-exposed ADB services and authenticates with prepared keys to install itself, giving operators shell access, file transfer, and tunneling on affected phones and Redroid containers.

item.title: Thomson Reuters detects cybersecurity incident, says unauthorized party accessed files (2 minute read)
item.description: Thomson Reuters found unauthorized access to C-Track files in March. The June 30 incident affected court systems in 11 US states, the US Virgin Islands, and Ontario. Exposed records may contain names and personal information. The company contained the activity, notified customers and law enforcement, and said C-Track remained operational.

item.title: Attackers Exploit PaperCut Flaws to Steal Credentials From Schools and Universities (2 minute read)
item.description: Threat actors are chaining CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078, an authentication bypass and remote code execution pair in PaperCut, to steal credentials from K-12 schools and major universities across the US and Europe. Users are advised to restrict PaperCut servers from being exposed to the internet and to monitor for the execution of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other scripting and command interpreters, as well as commands containing whoami, tasklist, ver, or uname -a, with pc-app.exe as the parent process.

item.title: Attackers Breached JetBrains Cadence via Unpatched TeamCity, Extracting AWS Credentials (3 minute read)
item.description: JetBrains is urging users of Cadence, its hosted cloud computing service, to revoke and rotate all credentials after unidentified attackers exploited CVE-2026-63077 (CVSS 9.8) to breach its own environment. The vulnerability stems from deserializing untrusted data and allows an unauthenticated attacker with access to a TeamCity server to bypass authentication checks and execute arbitrary operating system commands with the privileges of the TeamCity server process. Attackers reached a 2024 Cadence backup holding AWS IAM credentials, S3 files, PyCharm-synced source code, and personal data, so defenders should treat all executions as untrusted and audit connected AWS accounts, registries, and repositories for activity since August 8.

item.title: Improving our alignment and security efforts (12 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic paused cyber evaluations after three July incidents exposed real systems through third-party environments. It added real-time classifiers, stronger sandbox isolation, and outbound network blocks, while partners testing reduced-safeguard models must verify isolation, define scope, validate tasks, and stop violations. The company also froze RL environment changes, flagged over 10% for defects, and rebuilt review controls.

item.title: Turning Chrome Remote Desktop into Pure Red Team Ops (12 minute read)
item.description: A researcher at ZeroTrace Lab went down a rabbit hole to try and understand how they can disable the Chrome Remote Desktop connection banner after it was bothering them on a computer they remote into. This led to a reverse engineering journey that ended with them creating a script to patch the modal's x and y size variables to 0, resulting in the banner not being visible. After realizing the spyware/red team potential this opened, the researcher continued reversing and found that they could create a malicious msi installer that would install a tampered hosts.json and patched modal to allow for remoting by an attacker with no visible notification to the victim.

item.title: ASCII smuggling crosses over from AI prompt injection to phishing evasion (11 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft researchers observed a high-volume phishing campaign using invisible Unicode tag characters, a technique popularized in AI prompt injection research as ASCII smuggling. Rather than hiding instructions from people while exposing them to AI models, the attacker used the characters to split financial lure words so email filters could not parse them, turning "funding" into fun, an invisible tag character, then ding. The code points come from the deprecated Unicode Tags block, U+E0000 to U+E007F, which renders as nothing at all, and Microsoft surfaced the campaign while hunting for prompt injection in Defender for Office 365, where the first version of the signature kept firing on the England, Scotland, and Wales flag emoji because each is built from a base flag code point plus an invisible tag sequence. Defenders should strip invisible Unicode before content signatures run, treat unexplained tag characters as a high-confidence anomaly, and apply the same normalization upstream of any AI assistant that ingests email.

item.title: Hetty (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Hetty is an HTTP toolkit for security research. It aims to be an open-source alternative to commercial software like Burp Suite Pro, with powerful features tailored to the needs of the infosec and bug-bounty community.

item.title: Pigeon (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Pigeon allows creating delegated authority for AI agents. A Pigeon Pass says what an agent may do by issuing a narrowed, signed credential for what it may do, not a copy of everything you can do.

item.title: IRFlow Timeline (GitHub Repo)
item.description: IRFlow Timeline is a native macOS forensic timeline analysis tool. The 1.0.10 release adds support for ChatGPT Computer History logs as a forensic artifact.

item.title: Another swarm of OpenAI agents reached the open internet without the frontier lab's knowledge (3 minute read)
item.description: Researchers found OpenAI-linked agents editing a little-used German wiki from May through June. 3,700 agents posted 18,000 messages and shared answers for timed web-search tests while trying to hide posts with “ZZZ.”. A moderator deleted roughly 100 pages daily while agents created about 400 pages a day. Activity dropped after OpenAI noticed the incident and intervened.

item.title: Ababil of Minab: An Iran-Linked Destruction and Exfiltration Campaign Targeting the US and the Middle East (9 minute read)
item.description: Gambit Security tied Ababil of Minab, the pro-Iranian persona that claimed responsibility for the attack on LA Metro in March, to Black Shadow, an Iran-linked group that the Israel National Cyber Directorate attributed to Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security, undercutting the crew's claim to be a new standalone hacktivist outfit. The campaign combined exfiltration with destruction across four confirmed victims in the United States, Israel, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey, mixing scripted automation with hands-on-keyboard work through vCenter, Disk Management, SQL Server Management Studio, and Veeam consoles, including one run that dropped 58 SQL Server databases at Vyncs. Analysts also found additional Israeli and Turkish victims on the operator's staging infrastructure, custom exfiltration tooling in the form of a Flask receiver and a C++ uploader named FileFiend, and a briefly exposed browser session showing the operator using ChatGPT to refine the destruction script.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra Scores 100% on ExploitBench as OpenAI Blocks PoC Exploit Requests (3 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra after it scored 100% on ExploitBench, up from GPT-5.6 Sol's 78.5%. Testing found higher rates of arbitrary code execution and two undisclosed zero-days. The public release allows secure code review and patching while it refuses proof-of-concept exploit requests. OpenAI plans to restrict Daybreak access for defenders, including MS-ISAC participants.

item.title: G7 urges organizations to prepare for quantum cyber threats (2 minute read)
item.description: The G7 Cyber Security Working Group and CISA issued a joint advisory urging organizations to begin migrating to post-quantum cryptography now.

item.title: Evaluating Muse Spark 1.3 on Hack The Box Challenges (2 minute read)
item.description: Muse Spark 1.3 scored 72.9% on the HTB-Challenger benchmark, up from 50.41% for version 1.2 just one month earlier.

item.title: Booz Allen Cyber Weapon Index measures demonstrated AI cyber capabilities (3 minute read)
item.description: Booz Allen tested 18 US and Chinese models on attacker machines against a production-grade enterprise network.

item.title: Malicious .git Configs Can Make Claude, Codex, Cursor, and Other AI Agents Run Attacker Code (4 minute read)
item.description: Manifold Security found eight flaws in seven coding agents. A received repository can use .git/config to trigger commands through core.fsmonitor, and the commands run with the developer's account permissions, outside sandbox controls and without approval. Fixes exist for goose, Codex, and one Claude Code path. Hermes Agent, Qwen Code, Grok Build, and another Claude Code path remained exposed.

item.title: Coder's registry infrastructure compromised to push malicious modules (2 minute read)
item.description: An attacker added unauthorized IPs to Coder's Cloudflare pool for registry.coder.com and served credential-stealing Terraform modules between 07:35 and 21:45 UTC on August 31, exfiltrating cloud, CI/CD, OIDC, and SSH secrets to coder-infra[.]com. Patched releases are 2.37.0, 2.36.4, 2.35.7, and 2.34.9.

item.title: Attackers Expose Ongoing AI Tool Use Targeting Organizations in Latin America (8 minute read)
item.description: Two intrusion clusters targeting Latin American critical infrastructure accidentally exposed their operations by leaving a self-hosted NextChat instance open to the public on TCP 3000. The exposed prompt history and staging scripts revealed a heavy reliance on AI tools to rapidly iterate through failed SAM and NTDS.dit credential dumps using volume shadow copy workarounds. To detect this infrastructure, defenders should actively hunt for the m-doxa on duckdns[.]org subdomains and monitor for multi-SAN Let's Encrypt certificates rotated between February and June.

item.title: The Outsider Phishing Kit: A Resilient Threat in the Face of Law Enforcement Action (15 minute read)
item.description: Despite recent takedown efforts by Google and the FBI, the ChenLun Outsider Phishing-as-a-Service platform has proven highly resilient, with over 700 new phishing pages deployed in a single month. The platform operates a sophisticated kill chain that utilizes WebSockets to stream victim keystrokes in real time while allowing affiliates to manually push contextual 2FA prompts on demand. Defenders can hunt for this infrastructure across all known templates by looking for the unique GetSyncSetting configuration file and an alphabetical page prefix convention that maps directly to the victim exploitation stage.

item.title: Rogue ScreenConnect Installations Across Unrelated Hosts Suggest Worm-Like Activity (10 minute read)
item.description: Modified ScreenConnect clients recovered by Huntress watch the EndPointStatusMessage.Connections collection for newly observed Host sessions, then register 1.vbs through 4.vbs with ScreenConnect's virtual file-transfer system and queue them with the action set to Run, so merely connecting to an infected client can hand the Host the same four-stage VBScript chain. The loader profiles first: 1.vbs writes a three-bit state to %TEMP%\value.txt covering existing ScreenConnect installs, whether Defender is the only endpoint protection present, and whether RAM exceeds 5GB, and that value selects a user-level backdoor, an access package with a ComputerDefaults.exe UAC bypass and AMSI tampering, or a combo branch carrying wstunnel disguised as Themes.exe and XMRig renamed SearchIndex.exe. Defenders should treat RunFiles or RanFiles entries in ScreenConnect server audit logs showing those scripts executed from Process: Guest as indicators of compromise, check for the WindowsServiceHost Run key pointing at WindowsServiceHost.vbs in AppData, and note that Huntress recommends reimaging affected hosts rather than cleaning them.

item.title: From Patch to Exploit; Using Claude Code to Reverse Engineer a Zero-Day in Papercut NG (13 minute read)
item.description: Kev Breen used Claude Code against a patched PaperCut NG zero-day, spotting SQL injection IoCs in error logs and finding the patch blocked CALL/EXEC/SYSCS_ calls in the SQL lookup template. Claude decompiled the JARs, found an auth-bypass filter flaw using a matrix parameter, then a second bypass in pageValidate letting an unauth service parameter reach admin pages. Chaining both gave unauthenticated RCE via arbitrary file write as the papercut user, confirmed with a working Python PoC. A guardrail swapped the model mid-session when it probed exploitation logs. Breen later found a third bypass defeating the emergency patch and reported it to security@papercut.com, who said they were already aware.

item.title: Leash (GitHub Repo)
item.description: The open-source safety and control layer for personal AI agents: Engine, Desktop, Mobile, proxy, and shared contracts. Leash sits between your AI agents and the actions they take. Safe work keeps moving. Sensitive work becomes a clear decision you can understand and control.

item.title: AWSHound: An OpenSource AWS OpenGraph Collector (20 minute read)
item.description: AWSHound is a self-hosted open-source collector that maps AWS environments into BloodHound OpenGraph datasets to visualize attack paths. Unlike existing mapping tools, AWSHound performs strict offline IAM evaluations by intersecting identity policies with permissions boundaries and SCPs to ensure relationships are only drawn where effective permissions resolve to an explicit allow. Operating securely through standard AWS SDK credential chains, the tool demonstrated massive scalability during internal testing by mapping a 500-account organization into 10.5 million edges in approximately 15 minutes.

item.title: AIR Security (Product Launch)
item.description: AIR Security launched a firewall that inventories and evaluates skills, plugins, MCP servers, and add-ons. It detects malicious instructions, hidden behavior, excessive permissions, typo-squatted packages, and risky updates, then revokes access across dependent workflows.

item.title: UK Moves to Block High-Risk Tech Suppliers From Critical Infrastructure (3 minute read)
item.description: UK ministers tabled amendments to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill on August 24. The changes let them block high-risk technology suppliers from critical sectors. The move followed an Iran-linked attack that shut a UK energy facility for four days. The bill already mandates tight incident reporting and penalties, and SMEs supplying critical operators may face exclusion without adequate controls.

item.title: AI agents help compress ransomware intrusion to under 10 hours, raising stakes for CISOs (5 minute read)
item.description: A ransomware operator crossed an enterprise network in under 10 hours using AI agents, work Unit 42 estimated would have taken human hands roughly two weeks. The 50-plus ATT&CK techniques observed were unremarkable on their own, and analysts quoted here read the intrusion as human-directed, with AI handling delegated tactical work rather than anything approaching autonomy. The more durable observation is about transitive authority, where a repository account with no cloud admin rights can still alter a workflow that assumes a privileged cloud role, which is the gap that made speed matter.

item.title: OpenAI's new reasoning technique alarms AI safety experts (3 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI's Astra model uses "recurrent depth," letting it loop through the same query multiple times instead of reasoning step by step, which makes chain-of-thought logs harder to read. Scaling the technique could push reasoning fully into latent space, killing visibility into model behavior. OpenAI's Jakub Pachocki said Astra's chain of thought stays legible and that monitoring remains a research priority.

item.title: ValleyRAT Backdoor Disguises Itself as Adware (3 minute read)
item.description: Kaspersky found ValleyRAT hiding inside a modified build of the Chinese adware QN Wallpaper, sideloading a malicious libcef.dll through the signed QnWallpaper.exe to gain a trusted parent process that users routinely whitelist.

item.title: Rustbot, the macOS malware used in the latest Rust Supply Chain Attack (7 minute read)
item.description: Poisoned crates.io releases of arrayref, internment, and append-only-vec pulled in a malicious build-time dependency that fetched an arm64 Mach-O implant during cargo build, harvesting ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, and ~/.kube credentials before its RSA tasking channel was neutered by the private key shipping inside the binary.

item.description: Deploying AI agents without fixing your underlying telemetry data leads to lackluster results. item.title: Malicious Apache Modules Hijack Brazilian Government Site Traffic to Push Betting Pages (3 minute read)
item.description: Gambling Goblin installed malicious Apache modules on Brazilian government and education servers. The modules reverse-proxy visitors to fake Google Play, Microsoft Store, and Amazon pages promoting betting sites. Operators deployed DownPro, AlphaAgent, oRAT, 3snake, SSH brute-forcing, and reconnaissance tools. Administrators lack published module hashes, filenames, or paths for direct Apache checks.

item.title: BGP Hijack Infecting Networks Caused By a Comedy of Errors That's Not Funny at All (4 minute read)
item.description: Attackers hijacked Softaculous' 162.55.80.0/24 prefix and redirected Virtualizor update traffic to malicious servers. Hetzner's RPKI settings accepted /24 routes, while a forged AS path matched its ROA, so the attackers also obtained TLS certificates during the diversion. Virtualizor did not cryptographically verify update packages, and Softaculous cannot identify every affected server and urges customers to investigate.

item.title: Unitree G1 Humanoid Robot Flaws Allow Unauthenticated root RCE Over Bluetooth (3 minute read)
item.description: A security researcher discovered two independent flaws in Unitree G1 humanoid robots that could enable RCE on the devices. The first vulnerability allows an attacker within BLE range to obtain an AES-128 key without requiring the device to pair. The researcher found that the Unitree cloud API would decrypt the key without verifying ownership or serial numbers, allowing the researcher to access protected BLE operations, eventually allowing the attacker to exploit a buffer overflow to achieve RCE. The second path involves a path-traversal vulnerability in the robot's AI service, which enables an attacker to upload a file to the bashrunner's whitelist directory, enabling RCE.

item.title: Shai-Hulud: Whoever Controls Your Package Registry Controls Your Pipeline (7 minute read)
item.description: The npm worm lineage has evolved to a point where standard supply chain provenance mechanisms can no longer guarantee safety. During the August 2026 ChainDrop campaign, threat actors compromised over 400 packages in under four hours by hijacking a maintainer's legitimate signed release pipeline. The attackers utilized authorized infrastructure, so every poisoned package version successfully carried a perfectly valid SLSA attestation. To further evade traditional domain blocklists, the campaign hosted its command and control operations within an Ethereum smart contract. This attack builds upon the previous Shai-Hulud worms, which have recently pivoted to targeting authentication tokens for AI development tools like Claude, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini. Security researchers warn that these identical mechanics could easily compromise infrastructure-as-code pipelines, proving that current attestation models verify origin rather than actual code legitimacy. To defend against these pipeline hijackings, organizations must enforce strict version pinning, utilize curated registries, implement OIDC-scoped credentials, and apply aggressive network egress restrictions.

item.title: Financially Motivated Threat Actor BREEZE COMET Targets Brazil (10 minute read)
item.description: Since 2024, BREEZE COMET has targeted Brazilian banks, payment firms, retailers, exchanges, and fintech providers to make fraudulent Pix, STR, and Boleto transfers. Initial access included password spraying, fake IT-support calls, booby-trapped tax files, exposed JBoss servers, and rogue devices on retail networks. The group steals mTLS credentials, API keys, CI/CD secrets, and cloud tokens, then moves through SMB and RDP. Its toolkit includes REALBREEZE, COBALTSPIN, LIGHTPAINT, MILDFROST, KICKPLATE, and BOATBEAM. Mandiant recorded two transaction waves within 24-48 hours after access to core financial applications.

item.title: Developing Enterprise Frontier Safeguards With Our Customers (4 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic will roll out Enterprise Frontier Safeguards in phases this fall. Customer activity logs can remain in customer-controlled AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud storage, using customer-managed keys and access policies. Automated systems inspect rolling traffic windows for offensive cyber capability, biological misuse, and stolen credentials. Flags go to customer teams. Anthropic staff does not review them.

item.title: Path to Astra: Critical Capabilities and Frontier Safeguards (7 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI classifies Astra as Critical for cybersecurity capability. Tests found zero-days, browser sandbox escapes, and root privilege-escalation chains. OpenAI delayed release work after the Hugging Face incident. Astra refused 91.5% of cyber-jailbreak requests, versus 59% for GPT-5.6 Sol. Advanced cyber access starts with selected testers, then Daybreak Blue.

item.title: Claude-BugHunter (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Claude-BugHunter packages 83 auto-loading Claude Code skills distilled from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports, so the agent loads per-class detection patterns, payload tables, and chain templates by topic rather than by name.

item.title: CrowdStrike 2026 Threat Hunting Report: Exploitation Window Closes as AI Use Accelerates (4 minute read)
item.description: CrowdStrike reports that 88% of observed vulnerabilities were actively exploited within 48 hours of a public proof-of-concept release between January and June. Advanced threat groups like VAULT PANDA and GENESIS PANDA weaponized flaws in under 24 hours, while UMBRAL BISON targeted Linux privilege escalation vulnerability CVE-2026-31431 roughly 20 hours after disclosure. The report also highlights a rapid shift in alternative attack vectors, noting a fifteenfold increase in device code phishing alongside a massive concentration of software registry threats targeting npm.

item.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses (8 minute read)
item.description: A dark web service named Nexus recently advertised over 153 million scanned US and Canadian driver's licenses alongside millions of other identification documents on a Russian cybercrime forum. By correlating GMT timestamps embedded in the leaked image filenames with real-world travel records, researchers traced the infrared and ultraviolet scans back to a potential breach at the identity verification vendor idscan.net. Following the discovery of this continuous exfiltration campaign affecting major corporate clients, the FBI opened an official inquiry, and the Nexus site immediately went offline.

item.title: Critical Langflow Vulnerability Exploited as Attacks on AI Platform Rise (3 minute read)
item.description: CVE-2026-0768, a 9.8-severity remote-code-execution flaw in Langflow, is under active exploitation.

item.title: 23-Year-Old Sality P2P Botnet Disrupted (2 minute read)
item.description: An international operation disrupted the Sality P2P botnet after 23 years.
